newsitem.title: UGANDA: Rwandan strongman meets Museveni in Uganda.
newsitem.headline: Rwandan strongman meets Museveni in Uganda.

text.p: Rwandan military strongman Paul Kagame met Ugandan President Yoweri Museveni in Kampala on Wednesday to discuss unrest in eastern Zaire, where rebels have taken control and thousands of Rwandans have gone missing.
Museveni's media adviser, John Nagenda, told Reuters that Kagame would probably continue the talks on Thursday and a Zairean government envoy might fly in to join them.
The Rwandan government has actively supported the rebels in eastern Zaire and Uganda has said it sympathises with them.
Kagame is Rwandan vice-president, defence minister and commander of the Rwanda Patriotic Army. In the late 1980s he was chief of military intelligence in the Ugandan army.
Opponents of the Rwandan and Ugandan government say they are planning to carve out a Tutsi state in central Africa, embracing Uganda, Rwanda and eastern Zaire.
Museveni, a Hima from western Uganda, has close ethnic links with the Tutsis who dominate the Rwandan army and with the Banyamulenge rebels in eastern Zaire.

But Nagenda said: "There is all this nonsense about there is going to be a Tutsilisation of the region, which is total and complete rubbish.... I would expect that the region would be talked about in general, rather than the Tutsi element of it."
Nagenda said the talks might also cover the regional sanctions imposed on Burundi after Tutsi military leader Pierre Buyoya overthrew an elected Hutu president in July.
"I would not be surprised if the Burundi issue also came up. Some people think the sanctions should be removed," he said.
